Lapland has no radiotherapy unit, so its patients are treated at OYS in Oulu: from Utsjoki, 676 km and 9.4 hours away, 15 breast sessions mean 16 nights away [S52, S60, S59].

1. The OYS head of radiotherapy could evaluate a single 8 Gy session as default for uncomplicated painful bone metastases: equal pain relief, more retreatment [S31, S30, S32, S62]. From Utsjoki, expected nights away fall from 6.2 to 2.4 [S60, S59, S30]. OYS's patient page names no bone schedule [S69]. Within 30 days, the radiotherapy team reviews and decides [S31, S30, S32, S62]. Goal 3: "National targets and key effectiveness indicators defined for agreed cancers" [S61].

2. The OYS breast lead could evaluate 5 sessions as default for eligible patients (whole breast or chest wall without nodal radiotherapy), non-inferior to 15 [S9, S11, S15, S14]. Distance is a reason to choose it: from Utsjoki, 6 nights away and 37 road hours instead of 16 and 75 [S60, S59]. Lapland-wide, it removes 445 nights away and 23,307 € of Kela costs (lower bound) yearly [S33, S57, S34, S35, S60]. OYS's breast page says a course lasts 1 to 4 weeks [S69]. Within 30 days, the breast team reviews and decides [S9, S11, S15, S14]. Goal 3: "Patients receive treatment within target times" [S25, S24].

3. Lapland's data lead, with OYS, could publish yearly schedule mix and radiotherapy use by distance band [S21, S22, S27]. Within 30 days, the OYS team decides what to report [S21, S16]. Goal 3: "Regional differences in treatment are available and used to steer services" [S26].

Limitations: centre-point distances, population-based allocation and an assumed schedule mix [S59, S57, S60, S16].
